decisions.quote: The returned results included 16 SNPs associated with FPG in the Meta-Analyses of Glucose and Insulin-related traits Consortium (MAGIC) study [2]. The MAGIC SNPs were supplemented by 13 additional SNPs from previously published GWASs (ESM Table 2) for a total of 29 SNPs that we attempted to replicate in our African-American cohort.

decisions.reason: Both the shipped row (873) and blind target 0 correctly identify the MAGIC meta-analysis by Dupuis et al. (2010), 'New genetic loci implicated in fasting glucose homeostasis and their impact on type 2 diabetes risk' (Nat Genet 42:105-116; ref. [2] and ESM Table 2), as a primary original GWAS whose 16 fasting plasma glucose (FPG) SNPs were re-tested in the HUFS African-American cohort.

decisions.quote: Of the 16 SNPs recently reported in the MAGIC metaanalysis of over 122,000 participants [2], 12 were available for testing in the HUFS dataset (ESM Table 2). We directly replicated three SNPs (rs2191349, rs11558471 and rs4506565) located in or near DGKB-TMEM195, SLC30A8 and TCF7L2 genes respectively (Table 1). We also replicated SNPs from other GWASs for FPG: rs2722425 within ZMAT4 (p value=0.024) as well as rs625643 (p value= 0.048), which is located in a functionally unknown region on chromosome 1 (Table 1). SNPs from the remaining studies that did not directly replicate are not shown.
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind codings agree on 'mixed'. Of the 12 directly testable MAGIC SNPs from Dupuis et al. (2010), 3 directly replicated (rs2191349 in DGKB-TMEM195, rs11558471 in SLC30A8, and rs4506565 in TCF7L2, p < 0.05 in Table 1) while the remaining 9 did not directly replicate; even including local LD-based replication in Table 2, only 6 MAGIC loci (adding G6PC2, GCKR, and MTNR1B) replicated while the remaining tested MAGIC loci (PROX1, ADCY5, SLC2A2, GLIS3, ADRA2A, CRY2, MADD) did not.

decisions.quote: Here, we conducted replication of published GWAS results for FPG in African-Americans from the metropolitan area of Washington DC, USA.
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind codings agree on 'replication'. The paper uses genotype and phenotype data from an independent sample of 927 unrelated non-diabetic African-American participants in the Howard University Family Study (HUFS) to re-test previously published GWAS SNP associations with fasting plasma glucose, including those reported by Dupuis et al. (2010).
